title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: difference from Arminius — not that elect can be saved while remaining unbelieving, but that faith/obedience is not antecedent election-motive from free will determining itself
pass_a_gloss: I answer: The discrimination of our sentence from the Arminian is not situated in this, that he establishes that the elect cannot be saved without the condition of faith and of obedience having been rendered, but we opine that they can be saved even if they remain unbelieving and rebellious unto God: but that he makes this condition of faith and of obedience an antecedent motive of election, and suspends this act of believing from free choice excited by the grace of God and as it were reduced unto a certain equilibrium, but determining itself before election, and thence procuring the Divine election.
pass_b_english: I answer: Our view does not differ from the Arminian in this — that he holds the elect cannot be saved without faith and obedience rendered, while we think they can be saved even if they stay unbelieving and rebellious to God. The difference is this: he makes that condition of faith and obedience an antecedent motive of election, and hangs the act of believing on free choice excited by God's grace and as it were brought to a certain balance, yet determining itself before election and thereby procuring divine election.
source_text: Respondeo: Non in eo situm est discrimen sententiae nostrae ab Arminiana, quod ille electos non posse salvari statuat absque praestita fidei et obedientiae conditione, nos autem opinemur eos servari posse etiamsi maneant infideles et Deo rebelles: sed quod ille hanc fidei et obedientiae conditionem facit antecedaneum electionis motivum, et hunc actum credendi suspendit a libero arbitrio per gratiam Dei excitato et quasi ad aequilibrium quoddam reducto, sed seipsum ante electionem determinante, et inde electionem Divinam procurante.
